STEP 3: after «ir», the place takes «a»: «Voy a Madrid», «Vamos a la playa». If the article is «el», the merge is mandatory: a + el = «al»: «Voy al cine», never «a el cine». STEP 4: to ask the destination, use «¿Adónde vas?» («where are you going?»). For the means of transport, use «en»: «Voy en metro», «Voy en coche»; and «a pie» for going on foot. STEP 5: «hacer», «poner» and «salir» are regular in every form except «yo», which gains a «g»: hago, pongo, salgo. The rest: haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen; pones, pone, ponemos, ponéis, ponen; sales, sale, salimos, salís, salen. STEP 6: use «hacer» for activities: «hacer la compra», «hacer deporte», «hacer los deberes», «hacer una pregunta». For weather, «hace calor», «hace frío». STEP 7: «poner» means to put or to place: «poner la mesa» means to set the table. «Salir» needs «de» for the place you're leaving («Salgo de casa»), and «con» for company («Salgo con Ana»). STEP 8: pronunciation: the «h» in «hago» and «hacer» is silent, the «g» in «hago» is hard (AH-go), and the «c» in «hacer» has the «th» sound used in Spain (ah-THEHR). In Latin America, «hacer» sounds like ah-SEHR.
topicos.comparacao: English «I do, I put, I go out» are all regular verbs, so the irregularity here — a «g» popping up only in the «yo» form — is genuinely new rather than something to map from English: hago, pongo, salgo. «Ir» also changes its whole stem the way English «go» becomes «went», just differently: voy, vas, va…

exemplos.ru: Hago la compra los sábados.
exemplos.pt: I do the grocery shopping on Saturdays.

exemplos.ru: Pongo la mesa para la cena.
exemplos.pt: I set the table for dinner.

exemplos.ru: Salgo de casa a las ocho.
exemplos.pt: I leave home at eight.

exemplos.ru: Vamos al cine el viernes.
exemplos.pt: We're going to the movies on Friday.

tabelas.titulo: hacer, poner, salir: only «yo» is irregular

erros.motivo: In «yo», the «c» becomes «g»: hago, never «hazo».
The «yo» form of «poner» is «pongo».
The «yo» form of «salir» is «salgo».
A destination needs «a»; «en» shows where you already are.
A + el merges into «al».

topicos.titulo: Five verbs you use every day
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «venir» (to come) does two things at once: in «yo» it gains a «g» (vengo), and in tú, él and ellos, the stem's «e» becomes «ie»: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen. The «e → ie» pattern gets a full, calm explanation in lesson 13. STEP 2: «decir» (to say) has «yo digo» and changes «e → i» in the stressed forms: digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen. STEP 3: «dar» (to give) is regular except in «yo»: doy, das, da, damos, dais, dan. Notice the «-oy» ending, just like «voy» and «estoy». STEP 4: «ver» (to see): veo, ves, ve, vemos, veis, ven. Only «yo» is irregular, and none of the other forms carry an accent mark. STEP 5: «saber» (to know): sé, sabes, sabe, sabemos, sabéis, saben. «Sé» carries an accent mark so it isn't confused with the pronoun «se» (as in «Se llama Ana»). STEP 6: «saber» + infinitive means «to know how to do something» (a learned skill): «Sé cocinar», «No sé nadar». With a fact, it just means «to know»: «Sé que vives en Sevilla». STEP 7: to lock these in, memorize the «yo» form of these verbs as one list: voy, hago, pongo, salgo, vengo, digo, doy, veo, sé — plus «tengo» and «estoy», which you already know. STEP 8: pronunciation: «vengo» sounds like BEN-go, with a hard «g»; «digo» sounds like DEE-go; «veo» has two separate vowels (beh-O).
topicos.comparacao: English «I come, I say, I give, I see, I know» are all irregular too, so the pattern of irregularity itself isn't surprising — it's just a different set of irregular forms to learn: vengo, digo, doy, veo, sé. The one real trap is the accent mark on «sé», which keeps it apart from the unrelated pronoun «se».

exemplos.ru: ¿Vienes a mi casa el sábado?
exemplos.pt: Are you coming to my house on Saturday?

exemplos.ru: Digo la verdad.
exemplos.pt: I'm telling the truth.

exemplos.ru: Doy un regalo a mi hermana.
exemplos.pt: I'm giving my sister a gift.

exemplos.ru: No veo bien sin gafas.
exemplos.pt: I can't see well without glasses.

exemplos.ru: Sé cocinar paella.
exemplos.pt: I know how to cook paella.

erros.motivo: «Saber» has the irregular form «sé» in «yo».
With «tú», the form is «vienes».
The «yo» form of «dar» is «doy».
With «tú», the form is «dices».
«Sé» (from saber) carries an accent mark; «se» with no accent is a different word.

topicos.titulo: Ver × mirar, decir × hablar and saber + infinitive
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «ver» means to perceive with your eyes, or to watch: «Veo una película», «Veo la tele». «Mirar» means to look at something attentively, to direct your eyes toward it: «Miro el mapa», «Miro por la ventana». STEP 2: «decir» means to say/tell something to someone: «Digo la verdad». «Hablar» means to speak a language or to converse: «Hablo español», «Hablamos de música». Don't swap the two: «Digo español» doesn't exist. STEP 3: «saber + infinitive» is a learned skill: «Sé conducir». To say something is possible right now, use «poder» (lesson 13). STEP 4: fixed expressions with «dar»: «dar un paseo» (to go for a walk), «dar las gracias» (to thank), «dar la mano» (to shake hands). STEP 5: to say you know a person or a place, don't use «saber» — use «conocer» (to be acquainted with), which comes up later. For facts and information, use «saber»: «Sé tu nombre». STEP 6: important false friend: «asistir» in Spanish means «to be present»: «asistir a clase», «asistir a un concierto». To watch a movie, use «ver una película».
topicos.comparacao: English «to watch» and «to look» also split roughly the way «ver» and «mirar» do, which helps — the harder trap is «asistir», which looks like «assist» or «attend as a spectator» but actually means «to be present» at an event («asisto a la reunión»), while a movie is something you «ver» (watch). The same logic covers «decir» vs. «hablar»: English says «tell the truth», and Spanish matches that exactly with «decir la verdad».

tabela.sentido: to perceive, to watch (TV, a movie)
to speak a language, to converse
to know how to do something

erros.motivo: To state a fact, use «decir».
«Asistir a» means to be present at an event; a movie is something you «ver».
To direct your gaze attentively, use «mirar».
A learned skill needs «saber».

topicos.aulaTitulo: Querer, poder, deber and tener que
topicos.titulo: Querer and poder: the vowel that changes
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: you already used «quiero» and «quisiera» in lesson 8. Now you'll see the whole verb. In «querer», whenever the stress falls on the stem, the «e» becomes «ie»: quiero, quieres, quiere, quieren. STEP 2: the same thing happens in «poder» with the «o», which becomes «ue»: puedo, puedes, puede, pueden. STEP 3: the change applies to yo, tú, él/ella/usted and ellos/ustedes. In «nosotros» and «vosotros», the stress falls on the ending, so the stem stays as it is: queremos, queréis; podemos, podéis. Picture a boot shape that covers four forms and leaves two out. STEP 4: «ie» and «ue» are diphthongs — they sound like a single syllable, «KYEH-ro» and «PWEH-do», with the vowels never pulled apart. STEP 5: the infinitive follows «querer» and «poder» directly, with no preposition: «Quiero comer», «Puedo ayudar». STEP 6: «querer» + noun means to want something: «Quiero un café». With a person, it takes «a» (the personal a): «Quiero a mi abuela» means you love her dearly. STEP 7: «poder» expresses possibility, ability and permission. To ask permission: «¿Puedo entrar?». To ask a favor: «¿Puedes repetir?» (tú) or «¿Puede repetir, por favor?» (usted). STEP 8: «poder» isn't the same as «saber»: «Sé nadar» (I learned how to swim) versus «Hoy no puedo nadar» (today, for some reason, I can't / I'm not able to).
topicos.comparacao: English «I want» and «I can» never change their vowel at all, so this is new ground rather than something to transfer. The pattern itself, though, is very regular once you see the «boot» shape: four forms change («quiero, quieres, quiere, quieren» / «puedo, puedes, puede, pueden»), and the two «we/you-all» forms stay exactly like the infinitive stem.

exemplos.ru: Quiero aprender español.
exemplos.pt: I want to learn Spanish.

exemplos.ru: ¿Quieres un café?
exemplos.pt: Do you want a coffee?

exemplos.ru: No puedo venir hoy.
exemplos.pt: I can't come today.

exemplos.ru: ¿Puedo entrar?
exemplos.pt: May I come in?

exemplos.ru: ¿Puede repetir, por favor?
exemplos.pt: Could you repeat that, please? (usted)

exemplos.ru: Queremos viajar en verano.
exemplos.pt: We want to travel in the summer.

erros.motivo: The stem's «e» becomes «ie» in «yo».
The stem's «o» becomes «ue» in «yo».
In «nosotros», the stem doesn't change.
The infinitive follows «querer» directly, with no preposition.
The infinitive follows «poder» directly, with no preposition.

topicos.aulaTitulo: Querer, poder, deber and tener que
topicos.titulo: Deber, tener que, hay que, and the «boot» in other verbs
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «deber» (should, ought to) is regular: debo, debes, debe, debemos, debéis, deben. The infinitive follows it: «Debes dormir más» (it's advisable). STEP 2: «tener que» + infinitive is a concrete obligation or need: «Tengo que trabajar hoy». «Tener» has «tengo» and changes e → ie: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. It's always written with «que»; «tener de» doesn't exist. STEP 3: «hay que» + infinitive is a general obligation, with no subject: «Hay que pagar en la caja». The form «hay» never changes. STEP 4: a rule of thumb: «debo» for moral duty or advice, «tengo que» for what circumstances require of you specifically, «hay que» for what applies to everyone. STEP 5: the vowel change you saw in «querer» and «poder» shows up in many other verbs, with the same boot shape: e → ie (empezar: empiezo; pensar: pienso; preferir: prefiero; entender: entiendo), o → ue (volver: vuelvo; dormir: duermo; encontrar: encuentro; costar: cuesta), and u → ue (jugar: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan). STEP 6: use them with these structures: «empezar a + infinitive» (to start doing something), «pensar + infinitive» (to intend to), «volver a + infinitive» (to do again), «preferir + infinitive», «jugar al + sport» (jugar al fútbol, al tenis). STEP 7: not every verb changes its vowel. «Comer», «vivir», «hablar» and «salir» don't change; you'll pick up the list of verbs that do, little by little. When in doubt, listen for it — it's what the dictionary flags with «(ie)» or «(ue)».
topicos.comparacao: English has nothing like this vowel-swap pattern — «I start, I think, I prefer, I sleep, I play» stay exactly the same in every form — so the «boot» shape is new grammar to learn rather than something transferable. «Tener que» maps closely onto English «have to», and «hay que» onto the impersonal «one has to / it's necessary to», with no subject attached either way.

exemplos.ru: La clase empieza a las nueve.
exemplos.pt: Class starts at nine.

exemplos.ru: Pienso viajar en agosto.
exemplos.pt: I'm thinking of traveling in August.

exemplos.ru: Prefiero el té.
exemplos.pt: I prefer tea.

exemplos.ru: Duermo ocho horas.
exemplos.pt: I sleep eight hours.

exemplos.ru: Juego al tenis los domingos.
exemplos.pt: I play tennis on Sundays.

erros.motivo: Obligation is formed with «tener que».

erros.errado: Empezo a trabajar a las ocho.
erros.certo: Empiezo a trabajar a las ocho.
erros.motivo: The stem's «e» becomes «ie» in «yo».
In «nosotros», the stem doesn't change.
«Jugar» changes u → ue.
«Hay que» is impersonal and has no subject.

topicos.aulaTitulo: Querer, poder, deber and tener que
topicos.titulo: Polite set phrases with querer and poder
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask permission, use «¿Puedo + infinitive?»: «¿Puedo pasar?», «¿Puedo sentarme aquí?». STEP 2: to ask someone a favor: «¿Puedes + infinitive?» (tú), «¿Puede + infinitive?» (usted), «¿Podéis + infinitive?» (vosotros, Spain). STEP 3: to offer something: «¿Quieres un café?», «¿Quiere agua?» (usted). STEP 4: to accept: «Sí, claro», «Vale» (very common in Spain; in Latin America, «dale», «bueno» or «de acuerdo» are more common). STEP 5: to decline gently: «Lo siento, no puedo. Tengo que trabajar». Give the reason. STEP 6: to ask for something more softly, use «quisiera» (lesson 8) or «me gustaría», which you'll see at the A2 level: «Quisiera un café, por favor». STEP 7: watch «esperar»: it covers both «to wait for» («Espero el autobús») and «to hope». Sentences like «Espero que vengas» need the subjunctive, which comes at B1.
topicos.comparacao: English «may I come in?» and «can you repeat that?» use the same basic structure Spanish does. The difference is that in Spanish, the level of formality («tú» or «usted») changes the verb's actual form: «¿Puedes ayudar?» (tú) versus «¿Puede ayudar?» (usted) — English «can you help?» stays the same either way.

tabela.formula: Lo siento, no puedo. Tengo que…
tabela.exemplo: Lo siento, no puedo. Tengo que estudiar.

erros.motivo: The question opens with «¿».

erros.errado: ¿Puedo abrir la ventana? (asking the other person to open it)
erros.motivo: «Puedo» means you're the one who's able to; to ask someone else, use «puedes» or «puede».

erros.errado: No quiero ir porque tengo que de trabajar.
erros.certo: No quiero ir porque tengo que trabajar.
erros.motivo: No «de» after «tener que».
«Vale» accepts; to decline, apologize and explain.

topicos.titulo: Reflexive verbs and the pronouns me, te, se, nos, os, se
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: a reflexive verb is one where the action comes back onto the person doing it: I wash myself, I get myself up. In the infinitive it ends in «-se»: «levantarse», «ducharse». STEP 2: in a sentence, each person has its own pronoun, placed BEFORE the conjugated verb: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, os levantáis, se levantan. STEP 3: the pronoun agrees with the subject: «Yo me levanto», «Nosotros nos levantamos». You can't say «yo se levanta». STEP 4: «ducharse» and «lavarse» are regular. But some reflexives change their stem vowel, as you saw in lesson 13: acostarse (me acuesto), despertarse (me despierto), dormirse (me duermo) and, with e → i, vestirse (me visto, te vistes, se viste, nos vestimos, os vestís, se visten). STEP 5: with a second verb, the pronoun can go either before the conjugated verb or stuck onto the infinitive, with no hyphen: «Me quiero levantar» or «Quiero levantarme»; «Tengo que ducharme» or «Me tengo que duchar». Pick whichever sounds more natural to you. STEP 6: with a negative, «no» comes before the pronoun: «No me levanto temprano». STEP 7: body parts and clothes take the article, not the possessive: «Me lavo las manos», «Me peino el pelo». STEP 8: many verbs change meaning with the pronoun: «lavar» (to wash something) versus «lavarse» (to wash oneself); «acostar» (to put someone else to bed) versus «acostarse» (to go to bed oneself); «dormir» (to sleep) versus «dormirse» (to fall asleep).
topicos.comparacao: English also marks reflexive action with a pronoun, but it comes AFTER the verb and is often dropped or replaced by context («I get up», not «I get myself up»; «I wake up», not «I wake myself up»). In Spanish the pronoun is required and always comes BEFORE the conjugated verb: «me levanto», never «levanto» alone. Without it, the sentence is wrong or changes its meaning entirely.

exemplos.ru: Me despierto a las siete y media.
exemplos.pt: I wake up at seven thirty.

exemplos.ru: Me ducho antes de desayunar.
exemplos.pt: I shower before having breakfast.

exemplos.ru: Mi hermano se acuesta muy tarde.
exemplos.pt: My brother goes to sleep very late.

exemplos.ru: No me levanto temprano los domingos.
exemplos.pt: I don't get up early on Sundays.

tabelas.titulo: Three reflexives with a stem-vowel change

erros.certo: Yo me levanto a las siete.
erros.motivo: The pronoun «me» is required in Spanish.
The pronoun comes before the conjugated verb.
The pronoun agrees with the subject: «nosotros» calls for «nos».
With body parts, you use the article.
In «nosotros», the stem doesn't change.

topicos.titulo: Narrating your day: sequence, clock time, and frequency
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to put actions in order, use «primero» (first), «luego» or «después» (then, afterward), «por último» (finally). After «antes de» and «después de», the verb stays in the infinitive: «Antes de salir, desayuno» (before leaving, I have breakfast), «Después de cenar, veo la tele» (after dinner, I watch TV). STEP 2: clock times follow lesson 9's pattern: «a las ocho». With the exact hour, say «de la mañana», «de la tarde» or «de la noche»: «a las ocho de la mañana». Without a specific hour, use «por la mañana», «por la tarde», «por la noche»: «Estudio por la tarde». STEP 3: the trap: «la mañana» means morning, and «mañana» (with no article) means tomorrow. «Mañana por la mañana» means «tomorrow morning». STEP 4: frequency words: «todos los días» (every day), «casi siempre» (almost always), «normalmente» (usually), «a menudo» (often), «de vez en cuando» (now and then), «nunca» (never). Fixed days of the week take the article: «los lunes» (on Mondays), «los fines de semana» (on weekends). STEP 5: mealtimes. In Spain, the main midday meal tends to be later than it is in Brazil, and it's commonly called «comer» (la comida); «almorzar» is also heard. In Latin America, «almorzar» and «el almuerzo» are the usual words. «Desayunar» is to have breakfast, and «cenar» is to have dinner. «Merendar» is to have an afternoon snack. STEP 6: «almorzar» changes o → ue (almuerzo, almuerzas…), and the «z» becomes «c» only before «e». «Empezar» changes e → ie: «Empiezo a trabajar a las nueve» (I start work at nine). «Volver» changes o → ue: «Vuelvo a casa a las seis» (I get back home at six). STEP 7: false friend: «la cena» means dinner. A scene from a movie is «la escena», and the Christmas Eve dinner is «la cena de Nochebuena».
topicos.comparacao: English «dinner» can mean the main meal at any hour, which can be at noon in some dialects — Spanish keeps the midday meal and the evening meal as two separate words (comida/almuerzo versus cena) in every region. And where English «scene» and the word for an evening meal sound nothing alike, Spanish «cena» (dinner) and «escena» (scene) look deceptively similar on the page, which is exactly why it's flagged here as a false friend.

exemplos.ru: Almuerzo a las dos de la tarde.
exemplos.pt: I have lunch at two in the afternoon.

exemplos.ru: Mañana por la mañana tengo clase.
exemplos.pt: I have a class tomorrow morning.

exemplos.ru: Después de cenar, veo la tele.
exemplos.pt: After dinner, I watch TV.

exemplos.ru: Los sábados me acuesto tarde.
exemplos.pt: On Saturdays I go to sleep late.

linhas.exemplo: Todos los días me levanto a las siete.
De vez en cuando duermo la siesta.

erros.motivo: «Almorzar» changes o → ue in «yo».

erros.errado: Desayuno a las ocho a la mañana.
erros.certo: Desayuno a las ocho de la mañana.
erros.motivo: With an exact hour, you use «de la mañana».

erros.errado: Después de salgo, cierro la puerta.
erros.certo: Después de salir, cierro la puerta.
erros.motivo: After «antes de» and «después de», the verb goes in the infinitive.
«Todos» agrees with «días» (plural).
«Mañana» with no article means tomorrow; «la mañana» is the part of the day.

topicos.titulo: Ponerse, quedarse, irse, sentirse, and reciprocal action
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «ponerse» means to put something on yourself: «Me pongo el abrigo» (I put my coat on). To take it off, «quitarse»: «Me quito los zapatos» (I take my shoes off). STEP 2: «quedarse» means to stay somewhere: «Me quedo en casa» (I'm staying home). Watch out: «quedar» without the pronoun can mean to arrange to meet («Quedamos a las ocho»); with «se», it means to stay put. STEP 3: «irse» means to leave, to go away from where you are: «Me voy» (I'm leaving), «Nos vamos a casa» (we're heading home). Without the pronoun, «ir» just points to a destination: «Voy a casa» (I'm going home). STEP 4: «sentirse» + bien/mal/cansado: «Me siento bien» (I feel fine), «Se siente cansada» (she feels tired). The verb changes e → ie: me siento, te sientes, se siente, nos sentimos, os sentís, se sienten. STEP 5: when two or more people do the action to each other, the plural pronoun carries the sense of «to one another»: «Nos llamamos todos los días» (we call each other every day), «Se escriben mucho» (they write to each other a lot). STEP 6: if a sentence could be ambiguous (for example, «se miran» could mean «they look at themselves» or «they look at each other»), context settles it; to make the reciprocal meaning explicit, you can add «el uno al otro».
topicos.comparacao: English «to leave» and «to go» are two separate verbs, so the distinction feels familiar — but in Spanish it's the SAME verb, «ir», with the pronoun doing all the work: «me voy» is «I'm leaving / heading off», and «voy» alone is just «I'm going (somewhere)». The reciprocal sense, as in «nos vemos» (we see each other, see you around), has no separate verb in English either — English reaches for «each other» as separate words, where Spanish folds it straight into the pronoun.

erros.errado: Voy de casa a las seis. (leaving)
erros.certo: Me voy de casa a las seis.
erros.motivo: «Irse de» means to leave a place.
«Sentirse» is reflexive and needs the pronoun.
The place where you stay takes «en».
With clothes, you use the article.

topicos.aulaTitulo: Shopping, clothes, colours, este and ese
topicos.titulo: Colors and adjective agreement
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: the main colors are: rojo, azul, verde, amarillo, negro, blanco, gris, marrón, naranja and rosa. Say each one out loud, minding the sounds: «amarillo» sounds like «ah-mah-REE-lyo», and «azul» starts with the Castilian «th» sound (ah-THOOL). STEP 2: a color is an adjective and goes AFTER the noun: «una camisa blanca», «unos zapatos negros». You can't say «una blanca camisa». STEP 3: colors ending in «-o» have four forms: «rojo, roja, rojos, rojas». STEP 4: colors ending in «-e» or a consonant have only two: singular and plural. «Verde / verdes», «azul / azules» (the «z» becomes «c» before «-es»), «gris / grises», «marrón / marrones». STEP 5: «naranja» and «rosa» use the same form for masculine and feminine: «un abrigo naranja», «una falda rosa». STEP 6: to lighten or darken a color, add «claro» or «oscuro» to it, without changing the color word itself: «una camisa azul claro» (light blue), «un abrigo verde oscuro» (dark green). STEP 7: «pantalones» is plural: «unos pantalones», and the adjective agrees: «unos pantalones negros». You say «un pantalón» for a single piece. In Spain, «los vaqueros» are jeans; in Latin America you'll hear «los jeans». STEP 8: pronunciation: the «ll» in «amarillo» and «zapatillas» sounds like an English «y» in Spain; the «ch» in «chaqueta» sounds like English «ch»; the «z» in «zapatos» sounds like the Castilian «th».
topicos.comparacao: English colors also come after the noun when functioning as a true predicate, but as a modifier they normally come BEFORE it: «a white shirt», «black shoes» — exactly the mirror image of Spanish word order, where the color always trails the noun. English colors also never change their ending for gender or number («white shirt», «white shirts», whether the noun is masculine or feminine in another language), so the four-way or two-way agreement pattern here (rojo/roja/rojos/rojas) is new ground to learn.

erros.motivo: The color agrees in gender with «camisa».
The color agrees in number with «zapatos».
The color comes after the noun.
The plural of «azul» is «azules».
Singular: «azul». The plural is only for more than one item.

topicos.aulaTitulo: Shopping, clothes, colours, este and ese
topicos.titulo: Asking the price, trying things on, and paying
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask the price of one item, say «¿Cuánto cuesta?»; for several, «¿Cuánto cuestan?». «Costar» changes o → ue (cuesta, cuestan). For the total, «¿Cuánto es?». STEP 2: to ask for something, use «Quisiera…», «Busco…» or «¿Tiene…?»: «Busco una chaqueta negra» (I'm looking for a black jacket), «¿Tiene esto en una talla más grande?» (do you have this in a bigger size? — the word «más» is covered in lesson 26; for now just use the set phrase). With «tú», «¿Tienes…?». STEP 3: to try something on: «¿Puedo probarme esta camisa?» («probarse» changes o → ue: me pruebo). STEP 4: to say how it fits, use these set phrases: «Me queda bien» (it fits me well), «Me queda grande» (it's too big on me), «Me queda pequeño» (it's too small on me). STEP 5: to pay: «¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?» (can I pay by card?), «Pago en efectivo» (I'll pay cash). Note: «con tarjeta» (by card) and «en efectivo» (in cash). STEP 6: numbers 100 to 1000: cien, ciento uno, ciento dos… doscientos, trescientos, cuatrocientos, quinientos, seiscientos, setecientos, ochocientos, novecientos, mil. Exact hundred: «cien euros». With one more unit: «ciento cinco». STEP 7: the hundreds agree with the noun: «doscientos euros», but «doscientas camisas». STEP 8: prices: «9,50 €» is read as «nueve euros con cincuenta». In writing, Spain uses a comma for the cents. In other countries the currency and the way prices are read change: pesos, dollars, soles. STEP 9: pronunciation: «quinientos» sounds like kee-NYEN-tos; «cien» sounds like thyen; «ciento» sounds like THYEN-to.
topicos.comparacao: English «how much does it cost?» and «how much do they cost?» follow the same singular/plural logic Spanish does, so that part transfers directly. The round-hundred words are where the real difference shows up: English just says «five hundred, seven hundred, nine hundred» with no irregularity at all, while Spanish «quinientos» (not «cincocientos»), «setecientos» (not «sietecientos») and «novecientos» (not «nuevecientos») change shape in ways you simply have to memorize. And «cien» shifting to «ciento» the moment something follows it («ciento veinte») has no parallel in English «one hundred» at all.

exemplos.ru: ¿Cuánto cuestan estos zapatos? — Cuestan sesenta y cinco euros.
exemplos.pt: How much do these shoes cost? They cost sixty-five euros.

exemplos.ru: ¿Puedo probarme esta chaqueta?
exemplos.pt: Can I try on this coat?

exemplos.ru: Me queda grande.
exemplos.pt: It's too big on me.

exemplos.ru: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
exemplos.pt: Can I pay by card?

erros.motivo: One item: singular, «cuesta».
The verb is «probar(se)» and takes a «b».
With a unit following, «cien» becomes «ciento».
The hundreds agree in gender.
By card: «con»; cash: «en efectivo».

topicos.aulaTitulo: Shopping, clothes, colours, este and ese
topicos.titulo: The demonstratives: este, ese, and aquel
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: demonstratives point at something and signal distance. «Este» is for what's near the speaker; «ese» is for what's near the listener or a bit further away; «aquel» is for what's far from both. They pair with «aquí, ahí, allí». STEP 2: the forms of «este»: este, esta, estos, estas. Of «ese»: ese, esa, esos, esas. Of «aquel»: aquel, aquella, aquellos, aquellas. STEP 3: the demonstrative agrees with the noun in gender and number and comes before it: «esta camisa», «ese abrigo», «aquellos zapatos». STEP 4: without the noun, the demonstrative works as a pronoun: «Quiero este» (I want this one), «¿Cuánto cuesta esa?» (how much does that one cost?). Today it's written with no accent mark. STEP 5: «esto», «eso» and «aquello» are neuter: they're for an unidentified thing or an idea, and they never change form: «¿Qué es esto?» (what's this?), «Eso es caro» (that's expensive). STEP 6: there's no fusion with a preposition: «in this» is «en este», «of/from this» is «de esta», «in that» is «en ese». STEP 7: to choose between two things: «¿Cuál prefieres: este o ese?» (which do you prefer, this one or that one?) — lesson 16 covers more of this.
topicos.comparacao: English also has this near/far distinction, but collapses it into just two words, «this» and «that», where Spanish keeps three levels of distance (este/ese/aquel) tied to speaker, listener, and neither. And where English happily fuses a preposition straight onto the demonstrative-adjacent phrase («in this store»), Spanish never fuses the preposition onto the demonstrative itself: it's always «en esta tienda», never a contracted form, and «of that coat» is «de ese abrigo», word for word, with no shortcut.

exemplos.ru: Esta camisa es muy bonita.
exemplos.pt: This shirt is very pretty.

exemplos.ru: Ese abrigo es caro.
exemplos.pt: That coat is expensive.

exemplos.ru: Aquellos zapatos son baratos.
exemplos.pt: Those shoes over there are cheap.

exemplos.ru: ¿Qué es esto?
exemplos.pt: What is this?

exemplos.ru: Estoy en esta tienda.
exemplos.pt: I'm in this store.

tabela.distancia: near you, or a bit further (ahí)

erros.motivo: «Camisa» is feminine: «esta».
«Pantalones» is plural, and so is the verb.
For something you don't know the identity of, use the neuter «esto».
There's no fusion: «en» + «esta».
With no preposition, the demonstrative just points at the object.

topicos.titulo: Gustar works backward
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: in English we say «I like coffee» — I is the one doing the liking. In Spanish the logic runs the other way: it's as if the coffee pleases me. The thing that's liked is the subject of the verb, and the person who likes it is marked with a pronoun: «Me gusta el café» (literally, coffee pleases me). STEP 2: the pronouns are «me, te, le, nos, os, les»: me gusta (to me), te gusta (to you), le gusta (to him, her, usted), nos gusta (to us), os gusta (to you-all, Spain), les gusta (to them, ustedes). STEP 3: the verb agrees with the thing that's liked, not with the person who likes it: if it's one thing, «gusta»; if it's several, «gustan»: «Me gusta el cine» (I like the movies), «Me gustan los gatos» (I like cats). STEP 4: if what's liked is an action, the verb stays in the infinitive and «gustar» stays singular: «Me gusta cantar» (I like to sing), «Me gusta cantar y bailar» (I like to sing and dance). STEP 5: the article is required before the noun: «Me gusta el café», never «Me gusta café». STEP 6: to negate, «no» comes before the pronoun: «No me gusta el café». STEP 7: intensity goes after the verb: «Me gusta mucho» (I like it a lot), «Me gusta bastante» (I like it quite a bit), «No me gusta nada» (I don't like it at all). To say you love something, «Me encanta» (singular) and «Me encantan» (plural) are common. To say you hate it, «Odio» (regular, subject I) or «No soporto» (I can't stand). STEP 8: with people, «Me gusta Pablo» suggests romantic attraction. To say you like someone as a friend, say «Pablo me cae bien» (Pablo strikes me well / I get along with Pablo). For family and friends, use «Quiero mucho a mi abuela» (I love my grandmother dearly).
topicos.comparacao: The meaning of «to like» is the same as in English, but the sentence structure runs opposite directions. English «I like music» (subject: I) corresponds to Spanish «Me gusta la música» (subject: the music). The two most common wrong paths — treating «gustar» as if the liker were the subject («Yo gusto la música»), or inserting «de» as English «of» might suggest («Me gusta de música») — don't exist in Spanish: there's never a «de» after «gustar».

linhas.exemplo: Me gusta el cine. / Me gusta leer.
Me encanta bailar. / Me encantan las playas.

erros.motivo: The one who likes it is the pronoun «me»; the coffee is the subject.
The verb agrees with «los gatos»: plural.
The article is required in Spanish.
After «gustar» there's no «de»; the infinitive follows directly.
The negation goes before the pronoun.

topicos.titulo: Gustar with a named person, agreeing, and giving an opinion
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to say whose liking it is, add «a» plus the person, and repeat the pronoun: «A Pablo le gusta el cine» (Pablo likes the movies), «A mis padres les gustan los museos» (my parents like museums). The «le» and «les» can never be dropped. STEP 2: to emphasize or compare, use «a mí, a ti, a él, a ella, a usted, a nosotros, a vosotros, a ellos, a ustedes» + the pronoun: «A mí me gusta, ¿y a ti?» (I like it, how about you?). STEP 3: to agree with something positive, say «A mí también» or «Yo también» (me too). To agree with something negative, say «A mí tampoco» or «Yo tampoco» (me neither). STEP 4: to disagree: «A mí sí» (when the other person said no) and «A mí no» (when the other person said yes). Examples: «—Me gusta el té. —A mí también.» (I like tea. —Me too.), «—No me gusta la lluvia. —A mí tampoco.» (I don't like rain. —Me neither.), «—No me gusta el cine. —A mí sí.» (I don't like the movies. —I do.). STEP 5: «también» is never used with a negative: you can't say «a mí también no». For a negative, use «tampoco». STEP 6: to express a preference, say «Prefiero X a Y»: «Prefiero el té al café» (I prefer tea to coffee; a + el = al). With a verb: «Prefiero leer a ver la tele» (I prefer reading to watching TV). STEP 7: to give an opinion, use «Me parece + adjective»: «Me parece interesante» (it seems interesting to me), «Me parecen caros» (they seem expensive — plural). Also «Creo que + sentence» and «Para mí…» (for me, …). STEP 8: to say how interesting something is to you, «Me interesa(n)» works just like «gustar»: «Me interesan los idiomas» (languages interest me).
topicos.comparacao: English «me too» and «me neither» are the standard responses. Spanish «yo también» and «yo tampoco» work the same way, but with «gustar» it's more natural to say «a mí también» and «a mí tampoco», because «a mí» echoes the pronoun «me» already in the sentence. To disagree, we use «a mí sí» and «a mí no», which in English comes out as something like «I do» and «I don't».

exemplos.ru: A Pablo le gusta el cine.
exemplos.pt: Pablo likes the movies.

exemplos.ru: A mis padres les gustan los museos.
exemplos.pt: My parents like museums.

exemplos.ru: A mí me gusta correr, ¿y a ti?
exemplos.pt: I like running, how about you?

exemplos.ru: Me parece muy aburrido.
exemplos.pt: I find it really boring.

tabela.situacao: the other person likes it, you do too
tabela.resposta: A mí también.

tabela.situacao: the other person doesn't like it, neither do you
tabela.resposta: A mí tampoco.

tabela.situacao: the other person doesn't like it, you do
tabela.resposta: A mí sí.
tabela.exemplo: —No me gusta el pescado. —A mí sí.

tabela.situacao: the other person likes it, you don't
tabela.resposta: A mí no.
Prefiero X a Y.
Me parece + adjective.

erros.certo: A Pablo le gusta el cine.
erros.motivo: With «a + person», the pronoun «le» is required.

erros.errado: A mis padres le gustan los museos.
erros.certo: A mis padres les gustan los museos.
erros.motivo: The pronoun agrees with «mis padres»: «les».

erros.errado: —No me gusta el té. —A mí también.
erros.certo: —No me gusta el té. —A mí tampoco.
erros.motivo: To agree with a negative, use «tampoco».
In Spanish, you compare with «a»: «preferir X a Y».
«Parecer» agrees with what's being judged, in the plural.

topicos.titulo: Asking about likes, playing and performing
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask a friend: «¿Qué te gusta hacer?» (what do you like to do?), «¿Te gusta el cine?», «¿Qué música te gusta?». With «usted»: «¿Qué le gusta hacer?». STEP 2: to choose between two or more things, use «¿Cuál?» («which one») and «¿Cuáles?» («which ones»): «¿Cuál prefieres?», «¿Cuáles te gustan?». Before a noun, use «qué»: «¿Qué color prefieres?» (what color do you prefer?). STEP 3: «jugar a» + a game or sport: «Juego al fútbol» (I play soccer), «Jugamos a las cartas» (we play cards). «Tocar» + an instrument: «Toco la guitarra» (I play guitar), «Toca el piano» (he/she plays piano). You can't say «jugar la guitarra». STEP 4: «leer, ver series, salir con amigos, viajar, cocinar, ir al gimnasio, pasear» are free-time activities (to read, watch shows, go out with friends, travel, cook, go to the gym, go for a walk). STEP 5: false friends: «exquisito» means delicious, and a cake can be «exquisita»; to say something's odd or weird, use «raro» or «extraño». Watch out too for «divertido»: it covers both «fun» and «funny». STEP 6: a full answer keeps the dialogue going: «Me gusta mucho porque es relajante» (I like it a lot because it's relaxing). Add the reason with «porque».
topicos.comparacao: English «exquisite» and Spanish «exquisito» look like a direct match, but they aren't: English «exquisite» means finely made or refined, while Spanish «exquisito» simply means delicious — food, not craftsmanship. The word that actually means «odd, strange» in Spanish is «raro», which has no visual resemblance to any false-friend trap in English at all.

tabela.sentido: to play a sport or game

erros.motivo: Instruments are «played» with «tocar».
Sports and games are «played» with «jugar», plus «a».
«Exquisito» means delicious; for odd, use «raro».
Before a noun, you use «qué».

topicos.aulaTitulo: Pretérito perfecto: saying what you did today
topicos.titulo: The pretérito perfecto with haber
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: the «pretérito perfecto» talks about something that has already happened within a period that hasn't ended yet: today, this week, this month, this year; or something that still matters right now: «Ya he comido» (I've already eaten). STEP 2: build it in two parts: «haber» in the present + the past participle. The forms of «haber» are: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han. STEP 3: the past participle of -ar verbs ends in «-ado»: hablar → hablado, trabajar → trabajado. -er and -ir verbs end in «-ido»: comer → comido, vivir → vivido. STEP 4: the participle never changes — it has no gender and no number. You say «Ella ha comido» and «Ellas han comido»; only «haber» changes. STEP 5: nothing ever comes between «haber» and the participle. Negation and pronouns go before «haber»: «No he comido», «Me he levantado», «Ya me he duchado». The adverb «ya» goes either before «he» or after the participle: «Ya he comido» or «He comido ya», never «He ya comido». STEP 6: the most common markers are: «hoy, esta mañana, esta tarde, esta semana, este mes, este año, ya, todavía no, alguna vez, nunca, siempre». STEP 7: the most important thing to watch: English «I have eaten» can mean either a completed action in an unfinished period (which matches Spanish «he comido» closely) or an ongoing habit, and it never changes form for that difference — Spanish «he comido» is always the first kind, a single completed action: it means «I ate (today)» or «I've already eaten», never a recurring habit. Never use «tener» in place of «haber» to build this tense: «tengo comido» is not the pretérito perfecto. STEP 8: in Spain the pretérito perfecto is used for what happened today; in much of Latin America, the pretérito indefinido (which you'll see at A2) is preferred even for today: «Hoy comí».
topicos.comparacao: English «I have eaten» and Spanish «he comido» line up closely for a single completed action within a period that hasn't ended («I've eaten already» ↔ «ya he comido»), so that part transfers well. Where it gets tricky is that English «I have eaten» can also describe a repeated habit over time («I have eaten here for years»), a sense the Spanish pretérito perfecto never carries — Spanish always treats «he comido» as one finished event, equivalent to «I ate» or «I've already eaten», and nothing more.

exemplos.ru: Hoy he trabajado mucho.
exemplos.pt: I worked a lot today.

exemplos.ru: Esta semana hemos estudiado cinco horas.
exemplos.pt: This week we studied for five hours.

exemplos.ru: Ya he comido, gracias.
exemplos.pt: I've already eaten, thanks.

exemplos.ru: Todavía no he hablado con Ana.
exemplos.pt: I haven't talked to Ana yet.

exemplos.ru: Me he levantado muy pronto.
exemplos.pt: I got up very early.

erros.motivo: The auxiliary is «haber»; «tener» doesn't form this compound tense.
The auxiliary agrees with the subject: «ella ha».
The participle never changes.
The pronoun comes before «haber».
Nothing comes between «haber» and the participle.

topicos.aulaTitulo: Pretérito perfecto: saying what you did today
topicos.titulo: The participles that break the rule
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: a handful of very common verbs have an irregular participle. There aren't many, and you already know most of them from their infinitive. STEP 2: learn these first: hacer → hecho, decir → dicho, ver → visto, poner → puesto, escribir → escrito, abrir → abierto, volver → vuelto, romper → roto. STEP 3: compound verbs follow their base verb: «deshacer» → deshecho; «describir» → descrito; «devolver» → devuelto. STEP 4: verbs that are irregular in the present often have a perfectly regular participle: ir → ido, ser → sido, estar → estado, tener → tenido, dar → dado, saber → sabido, querer → querido, poder → podido, salir → salido, venir → venido. STEP 5: -er and -ir verbs whose stem ends in a vowel carry an accent on the «í» of the participle: leer → leído, creer → creído, oír → oído, traer → traído, caer → caído. STEP 6: an irregular participle is used exactly the same way: «Hoy he hecho la compra» (today I did the shopping), «Hemos visto una película» (we've watched a movie), «Han escrito un correo» (they've written an email). STEP 7: to practice, answer the question «¿Qué has hecho hoy?» always with «he + participle». STEP 8: in negative sentences with «todavía no», the participle stays exactly the same: «Todavía no he visto la película».
topicos.comparacao: English irregular past participles (seen, done, written, opened) are just as unpredictable as Spanish ones, so the habit of simply memorizing the irregular list transfers directly. The trap here is specific to Spanish: inventing a regular-looking form by false analogy with the infinitive — something like «he hacido» or «he escribido» — which isn't a mistake English speakers would make the same way, since English doesn't build its irregular participles off a predictable suffix pattern to begin with.

erros.motivo: «Hacer» has an irregular participle: «hecho».
«Escribir» has an irregular participle: «escrito».
«Abrir» has an irregular participle: «abierto».
«Ver» has an irregular participle: «visto».
The participle of «leer» carries an accent on the «í».

topicos.aulaTitulo: Pretérito perfecto: saying what you did today
topicos.titulo: Asking and answering about experiences
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask about a life experience, use «alguna vez»: «¿Has estado alguna vez en Madrid?» (have you ever been to Madrid?). STEP 2: possible answers: «Sí, he estado una vez / dos veces / muchas veces» (yes, I've been once / twice / many times) and «No, nunca he estado» or «No he estado nunca» (no, I've never been). STEP 3: to ask whether something has already happened: «¿Has comido ya?» (have you eaten yet?). Answers: «Sí, ya he comido» or «Todavía no he comido». STEP 4: to ask about today: «¿Qué has hecho hoy?» (what have you done today?). Answers with «he + participle». STEP 5: with «usted»: «¿Ha estado alguna vez en Brasil?»; with «vosotros» (Spain): «¿Habéis estado alguna vez en Brasil?». STEP 6: false friend: «asistir a» means to attend an event (a class, a concert, a meeting) — it has nothing to do with watching a movie: a movie is something you «ve» (see/watch). STEP 7: «perder» means to lose (something, the train, your keys) and follows the same pattern: «He perdido el tren» (I missed the train). Watch out: «perder» changes e → ie in the present (pierdo).
topicos.comparacao: Spanish «asistir a» looks like it should mean «to assist» or even «to watch», but it actually means «to attend» an event — a class, a concert, a meeting. The verb for watching a movie is simply «ver», the same verb used for seeing anything. The resemblance between «asistir» and English «assist» is the trap here, since the two words don't share that meaning at all.

tabela.resposta: Sí, he estado dos veces. / No, nunca he estado.
Sí, ya he comido. / Todavía no.
He trabajado y he ido al mercado.
Sí, he estado una vez.
No, nunca hemos estado.
No, todavía no he visto esta película.

erros.motivo: Movies are «watched» with «ver»; «asistir a» means to attend an event.
With «estar», the place takes «en».

erros.errado: Nunca no he estado en Madrid.
erros.motivo: With «nunca» before the verb, you don't use «no»; after the verb, you do: «No he estado nunca en Madrid».
The participle doesn't agree with the object.

topicos.titulo: All of A1 in one table
topicos.explicacao: This table sums up lessons 1 through 17. Reread one line at a time and say your own example out loud. If something feels off, go back to the lesson it points to or open the topic in the Grammar tab. The four trickiest points for English speakers are: the fully pronounced vowel (never reducing «e» and final «o» the way English does with unstressed vowels), the «j» and «th» sounds (z, ce, ci), «ser» versus «estar», and «gustar» working backward.

tabela.regra: vowels always clear; «j» = a strong h sound; «z, ce, ci» = th (Spain); «ñ», «ll», «rr»; silent «h»; the marks ¿ ? ¡ !; stressed syllable and the accent mark.
soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son; tú × usted; the adjective agrees; «muy»; «no» before the verb.
«Me llamo…», «Soy de… / Soy brasileño»; numbers from 0 to 20; age with «tener»: «Tengo veinte años».
hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan; questions with ¿dónde? ¿qué? ¿por qué?; «porque»; «muy» × «mucho»; the personal «a».
el, la, los, las, un, una, unos, unas; plural with -s and -es; «hay un café» (existence).
como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen; vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven.
mi, tu, su, nuestro, vuestro; mis, tus, sus; «mi hermana», «mis padres».

tabela.tema: Coffee, food, and numbers up to 100
tabela.regra: «Quiero…», «Quisiera…», «¿Qué desea?», «La cuenta, por favor»; numbers from 21 to 100.
«Es la una», «Son las dos y media»; days of the week; months; «el cinco de mayo».
estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están; «en, encima de, debajo de, al lado de, cerca de, lejos de».
«¿Dónde está…?», «Siga todo recto», «Gire a la derecha / a la izquierda».
voy, hago, pongo, salgo, vengo, digo, doy, veo, sé; ver × mirar; decir × hablar.
quiero, puedo; «tengo que», «debo», «hay que» + infinitive; stem-changing verbs.
me levanto, te levantas, se levanta; the pronoun before the verb; «antes de» and «después de» + infinitive.
the color agrees and comes after; «¿Cuánto cuesta?»; 100 to 1000; este, ese, aquel.
«Me gusta el cine», «Me gustan los gatos», «Me gusta cantar»; «a mí también / tampoco».
he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + participle; hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto.

topicos.titulo: The 18 most common A1 mistakes
topicos.explicacao: Read each pair out loud: first the wrong version, then the right one, then the rule. Mark the mistakes you still make and go back to the lesson named in the explanation.

erros.motivo: Age is said with «tener», not with «ser» (lesson 3).
Origin is said with «ser» (lessons 2 and 3).
After a verb, use «mucho»; «muy» only comes before an adjective or adverb (lesson 4).
A person as the object calls for the personal «a» (lesson 4).

erros.errado: Hay el libro en la mesa.
erros.certo: Hay un libro en la mesa. / El libro está en la mesa.
erros.motivo: «Hay» introduces something new, with an indefinite article; something already known uses «está» (lessons 5 and 10).
The place where someone is calls for «estar» (lesson 10).
Plural clock times take «son»; only «es la una» is singular (lesson 9).
a + el = al (lesson 12).
In «yo», the «c» becomes «g»: hago (lesson 12).
The stem's «e» becomes «ie» (lesson 13).
Obligation is formed with «tener que» (lesson 13).
The reflexive pronoun is required and comes first (lesson 14).
The color agrees in gender (lesson 15).
The demonstrative agrees with the noun (lesson 15).
The verb agrees with the thing that's liked (lesson 16).
The pretérito perfecto uses «haber», not «tener» (lesson 17).
Irregular participle: «escrito» (lesson 17).
Feelings like cold, hunger, or thirst use «tener», not «ser» — the reverse of English «I am cold».

topicos.titulo: Indefinido: -ar verbs
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: use the pretérito indefinido for something that happened and ended at a moment you can name: «ayer», «anoche», «el lunes», «en 2019», «hace dos días». STEP 2: for -ar verbs, drop the «-ar» from the infinitive and add these endings: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. «Hablar» becomes «hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron». STEP 3: the first person (yo) and the third person (él, ella, usted) carry a written accent: «hablé» and «habló». The accent marks the stressed syllable and also keeps the past apart from the present: «hablo» (I speak) versus «habló» (he/she spoke). STEP 4: in «nosotros», the indefinido of -ar verbs looks exactly like the present: «hablamos». Context settles it: «Ayer hablamos» is past, «Hablamos cada día» is a habit. STEP 5: «vosotros» (Spain) ends in «-asteis»: «hablasteis». In Latin America, «ustedes» uses «hablaron». STEP 6: the subject pronoun is almost always dropped, because the ending already says who it is: «Ayer cené en casa» (I had dinner at home yesterday). STEP 7: the indefinido has no connection to the present — the fact is closed off in the past. With «hoy», «esta semana» or «este año», which haven't ended yet, Spain prefers the pretérito perfecto from lesson 17: «Hoy he trabajado mucho». In much of Latin America people say «Hoy trabajé mucho» instead, since there the indefinido often takes over the perfecto's job.
topicos.comparacao: English's simple past («I talked», «you talked», «he talked») never changes shape for the subject at all, so the whole idea of six distinct person-endings is new ground, not something to carry over. The trickiest traps here are specific to Spanish spelling: the «-ó» ending (with no English equivalent at all), the «-aron» plural ending, and the «vosotros» form «hablasteis», which has no counterpart in English either since English marks no distinction between «you» singular and «you» plural. The written accent is another new habit: English never marks stress with an accent mark, but in Spanish it's what tells «hablo» (I speak, present) apart from «habló» (he/she spoke, past).

exemplos.ru: El año pasado viajé a Valencia.
exemplos.pt: Last year I traveled to Valencia.

exemplos.ru: Anoche cenamos en casa de Marta.
exemplos.pt: Last night we had dinner at Marta's place.

exemplos.ru: Mi hermano trabajó el sábado.
exemplos.pt: My brother worked on Saturday.

erros.motivo: With «ayer», the fact is finished: use the indefinido, not the present.
The ending for «él, ella» is «-ó».
The ending for «ellos» is «-aron».
With «tú», the ending is «-aste», with no final «s».
Without the accent, «hable» is a different verb form; the «yo» indefinido takes «-é».

topicos.titulo: Indefinido: -er, -ir, and spelling changes
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: -er and -ir verbs use the same endings in the indefinido: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. «Comer» becomes «comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron». «Vivir» becomes «viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivisteis, vivieron». STEP 2: the first person «-í» and the third person «-ió» carry an accent: «comí», «comió». STEP 3: in «nosotros», -ir verbs look just like the present («vivimos»), but -er verbs change: present «comemos», indefinido «comimos». STEP 4: watch the third-person ending closely: it's «comió», «vivió» — never anything resembling an English-style reduction. And the plural is «comieron», never «comeron». STEP 5: to keep the sound the same, some -ar verbs change their spelling only in «yo». Verbs ending in «-car» become «-qué» («buscar → busqué»), those in «-gar» become «-gué» («llegar → llegué»), and those in «-zar» become «-cé» («empezar → empecé»). STEP 6: when the stem ends in a vowel, the «i» between two vowels becomes «y» in the third person: «leer → leyó, leyeron». The other forms carry an accent on the «í»: «leí, leíste, leímos, leísteis». «Creer» (creyó) and «oír» (oyó) do the same thing. STEP 7: «salir» is irregular only in the present («salgo»); in the indefinido it's regular: «salí, saliste, salió». STEP 8: a few very common verbs (ser, ir, hacer, tener, decir, ver) are irregular in the indefinido. Those are saved for lesson 20.
topicos.comparacao: English past-tense verbs don't change their ending based on whether the root ends in a vowel or consonant, so the «i → y» spelling shift in «leyó», «creyó», «oyó» has no parallel to lean on — it's simply a Spanish spelling rule to learn on its own. The «-car/-gar/-zar» spelling changes (busqué, llegué, empecé) are the same kind of thing: a pattern that keeps the consonant sound stable in writing, with nothing in English's own spelling system to map it onto.

exemplos.ru: Anoche escribí un correo largo.
exemplos.pt: Last night I wrote a long email.

exemplos.ru: Llegué a casa a las nueve.
exemplos.pt: I got home at nine.

exemplos.ru: Ellos vivieron un año en Lima.
exemplos.pt: They lived in Lima for a year.

linhas.motivo: c + é would sound like «th»; «qu» keeps the «k» sound
g + é would sound like «h»; «gu» keeps the «g» sound
z is never written before «e»; it becomes «c»

erros.motivo: In the third person of -er and -ir verbs, the ending is «-ió».
The plural is «-ieron».
To keep the «g» sound, you write «gu» before the «é».

erros.errado: El año pasado empezé a estudiar.
erros.certo: El año pasado empecé a estudiar.
erros.motivo: You never write «z» before «e»; use «c» instead.
The «i» between two vowels becomes «y»: «leyó».

topicos.titulo: Indefinido or perfecto, and three false friends
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: think of the clock. If the period has already ended («ayer», «el lunes», «en 2019», «la semana pasada», «hace dos días»), use the indefinido: «Ayer compré pan» (yesterday I bought bread). STEP 2: if the period hasn't ended yet («hoy», «esta mañana», «esta semana», «este año»), Spain uses the pretérito perfecto: «Esta semana he trabajado mucho». STEP 3: in Latin America, the indefinido often takes the perfecto's place: «Esta semana trabajé mucho». Both versions are correct, each in its own region; pick one and stay consistent. STEP 4: to say «two days ago» about a past fact, put «hace» before the amount of time and nothing else: «Llegué hace dos días». You never say «hace dos días atrás». STEP 5: three false friends for talking about the past. «Cenar» and «la cena» mean «to have dinner» and «dinner» (the meal): «Cené a las ocho». «Un rato» means «a little while», not the rodent; the rodent is «ratón» (and «rata» is the bigger rat): «Esperé un rato» (I waited a little while). «Oficina» means «office» (the workplace): «Trabajé en la oficina».
topicos.comparacao: English makes no distinction at all between «I ate yesterday» and «I've eaten today» in terms of which past tense to reach for — the simple past covers the first and the present perfect the second, but nothing about English grammar maps directly onto the Spain/Latin-America split here. Spain keeps «Ayer comí» (indefinido) and «Hoy he comido» (perfecto) strictly separate by whether the time period is closed or still open; in Latin America that line is looser, and the indefinido covers both cases.

tabela.exemplo: El lunes pasado compré un libro.

tabela.marcador: la semana pasada, el año pasado, en 2019

erros.motivo: «Ayer» is a finished time: use the indefinido.
«Hace» already marks the past; «atrás» is redundant.

erros.errado: Hay un rato en la cocina.
erros.certo: Hay un ratón en la cocina.
erros.motivo: «Rato» means a little while; the rodent is «ratón».

erros.errado: Ayer trabajé en el escritorio de mi empresa.
erros.certo: Ayer trabajé en la oficina de mi empresa.
erros.motivo: «Escritorio» is the desk itself; the office as a place is «oficina».

topicos.titulo: Ser, ir, dar, ver, and hacer in the indefinido
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: a few very common verbs don't follow lesson 19's pattern. They have their own forms, and it's worth memorizing them as whole words. STEP 2: «ser» and «ir» share exactly the same form in the indefinido: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. The meaning comes from the rest of the sentence: «Fui a Madrid» (I went to Madrid, verb «ir») and «Fue un día largo» (it was a long day, verb «ser»). STEP 3: with «ir», the place follows «a»: «Fuimos a la playa», «Fui al médico» (a + el = al). Never with «en». STEP 4: «dar» and «ver» use the same -er/-ir endings but carry no written accent, because they're one-syllable words: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron; vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron. STEP 5: «hacer» swaps its stem for «hic-»; in the third person singular, the «c» becomes «z» to keep the sound: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. STEP 6: none of these forms carries a written accent: «fui», «fue», «di», «vi», «dio», «vio». Writing «fuí» or «vió» is a common mistake. STEP 7: in Latin America, these forms are the same. What changes is frequency: there, «Hoy fui al médico» sounds natural, while Spain tends to prefer «Hoy he ido al médico».
topicos.comparacao: English «went» covers both «ir» and, loosely, a sense of «was» in some idioms, but Spanish folding «ser» and «ir» into the exact same form (fui, fue, fuimos…) has no real English parallel — you have to rely entirely on context to tell them apart, the same way context (not form) tells «I was» from «I went» apart in English, just through different words rather than the same one. The spelling trap here is specific to Spanish: these one-syllable forms (fui, fue, di, vi, dio, vio) never carry a written accent, unlike the two-syllable-or-more regular endings from lesson 19 (hablé, habló) which do.

exemplos.ru: El domingo vi una película con mi primo.
exemplos.pt: On Sunday I watched a movie with my cousin.

exemplos.ru: Mi madre me dio un regalo.
exemplos.pt: My mother gave me a gift.

exemplos.ru: ¿Qué hicisteis el viernes?
exemplos.pt: What did you all do on Friday?

erros.motivo: «Fui» has one syllable and carries no written accent.
With «ir», the destination takes «a».
In the third person, the «c» becomes «z»: «hizo».
The «yo» form is «hice».
«Vio» has one syllable and carries no accent.

topicos.titulo: New stems: tener, estar, poder, poner, saber, querer, venir
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: a group of verbs changes its entire stem in the indefinido and uses its own set of endings: -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. STEP 2: none of these endings carries a written accent. Compare «hablé / habló» (regular, with an accent) and «tuve / tuvo» (irregular, with no accent). STEP 3: the stems to memorize: tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud-, poner → pus-, saber → sup-, querer → quis-, venir → vin-, hacer → hic- (from the earlier section). STEP 4: a full example: «tener»: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron. «Venir»: vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron. STEP 5: «estar» in the indefinido says where you were during a closed period: «Estuve en Lima una semana» (I was in Lima for a week). STEP 6: some of these verbs shift meaning in the indefinido, because the fact is a single point in time rather than an ongoing state. «Supe la noticia» means «I found out the news» (at that moment), not «I knew». «Pude venir» means «I managed to come», and «No pude venir» means «I wasn't able to come». «No quise venir» means «I refused to come», with the sense of actively declining. «Conocí a Ana» means «I met Ana (for the first time)», and «conocer» is actually regular in this tense. STEP 7: «tener que + infinitive» (lesson 13) in the past also uses the indefinido: «Tuve que trabajar el sábado». STEP 8: watch the «v»: «estuve» and «tuve» both have a «v», and so does «vine». «Estube» and «tubo» (which is actually the word for a pipe) are both mistakes.
topicos.comparacao: English has the same kind of irregular stem-swap in its own past tense — «go/went», «see/saw», «have/had» are just as unpredictable — so the habit of memorizing an irregular form as a whole word, rather than deriving it, transfers directly. What doesn't transfer is the meaning shift some of these verbs carry in Spanish: English «I knew» and «I could» describe ongoing states, with no separate form for a single, pinpoint moment the way Spanish «supe» (I found out, right then) and «pude» (I managed to, on that occasion) do. That's a real distinction to learn, not just a vocabulary item.

exemplos.ru: El jueves tuve un examen difícil.
exemplos.pt: On Thursday I had a hard exam.

exemplos.ru: Estuvimos una semana en Lisboa.
exemplos.pt: We stayed in Lisbon for a week.

exemplos.ru: Ayer supe la noticia por una amiga.
exemplos.pt: Yesterday I found out the news from a friend.

exemplos.ru: No pude ir a la fiesta.
exemplos.pt: I wasn't able to go to the party.

erros.motivo: The stem of «tener» in the indefinido is «tuv-».
«Estar» is spelled with a «v»: «estuv-».
These irregular forms carry no accent.

erros.errado: Ayer él viniró a mi casa.
erros.certo: Ayer él vino a mi casa.
erros.motivo: The third-person singular of «venir» is «vino», with no accent.
The stem of «saber» in the indefinido is «sup-».

topicos.titulo: Decir, traer, and verbs like pedir and dormir
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «decir» and «traer» have a stem with «j»: dij- and traj-. The endings are the usual ones, but the «i» drops after the «j»: the third-person plural ends in «-eron», not «-ieron». «Dijeron», «trajeron». STEP 2: decir: dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron. Traer: traje, trajiste, trajo, trajimos, trajisteis, trajeron. STEP 3: -ir verbs that change their stem vowel in the present (pedir → pido, dormir → duermo) also change in the indefinido, but only in the third person, singular and plural: «e» becomes «i» and «o» becomes «u». Pedir: pedí, pediste, pidió, pedimos, pedisteis, pidieron. Dormir: dormí, dormiste, durmió, dormimos, dormisteis, durmieron. STEP 4: the same thing happens with «seguir» (siguió), «servir» (sirvió), «repetir» (repitió), «preferir» (prefirió), «sentir» (sintió), «morir» (murió), and «divertirse» (se divirtió). STEP 5: two meaning traps. «Largo» means «long», not «large» — the word for «large» is «grande», and the word for «wide» is «ancho»: «Una calle ancha» (a wide street), «un viaje largo» (a long trip). And «vaso» means «glass» (the drinking kind), not a flower vase (which is «jarrón» or «maceta»): «Pedí un vaso de agua» (I asked for a glass of water).
topicos.comparacao: English past-tense verbs don't change shape between «he asked» and «they asked» — the whole stem-vowel-flip pattern here (e → i, o → u, only in the third person) is new ground with nothing to transfer from English. The real trap, though, is the false-friend pair «largo»/«large»: they look almost identical, but «largo» means «long» and has nothing to do with size or largeness, which is exactly the word an English speaker would reach for by mistake.

erros.motivo: After the «j», the ending is «-eron».
The stem of «traer» is «traj-».
In the third person, the «e» of «pedir» becomes «i».
In the third person, the «o» of «dormir» becomes «u».
«Largo» means long; width is «ancho».

topicos.titulo: Imperfecto: -ar, -er, and -ir
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: the pretérito imperfecto describes the past without saying when it started or when it ended. It's for what used to be habitual, for descriptions, and for the backdrop of a scene. «De niño vivía en Sevilla» (I lived there as a child — no telling how long). STEP 2: for -ar verbs, drop the «-ar» and add: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. «Hablar» becomes «hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban». STEP 3: for -er and -ir verbs, drop the ending and add: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. «Comer» becomes «comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían». «Vivir» becomes «vivía, vivías, vivía, vivíamos, vivíais, vivían». STEP 4: «yo» and «él, ella, usted» share the same form: «hablaba», «comía». When that's ambiguous, add the pronoun: «Yo vivía en Lima y ella vivía en Cusco». STEP 5: the written accent is required on «-ía» (always) and on «-ábamos» (nosotros, -ar). Without it, the pronunciation is wrong — there's no such word as «comia» in Spanish. STEP 6: -ar verbs are spelled with a «b» in «-aba». STEP 7: this tense is regular even for verbs that change their stem in the present: «dormir» becomes «dormía» (not «durmía»), «tener» becomes «tenía», «hacer» becomes «hacía». STEP 8: the typical markers are «de niño», «antes», «siempre», «cada día», «todos los veranos», «a menudo», «normalmente», «entonces», and «mientras».
topicos.comparacao: English has no dedicated conjugation for this tense at all — it leans on «used to» + infinitive («I used to live there») or just the plain simple past, with context doing all the work of signaling habit versus a one-off event. Spanish, by contrast, marks the distinction directly in the verb's own ending, so «hablaba» can never be mistaken for a single finished action the way English «I talked» can mean either a habit or a one-time event depending on what surrounds it. Because English gives you no verb-shape cue to lean on here, the endings themselves — and especially the written accent on «-ía» and «-ábamos» — are the part worth drilling hardest.

exemplos.ru: Antes trabajaba en un banco.
exemplos.pt: As a child I used to work at a bank.

exemplos.ru: De pequeña vivíamos cerca del mar.
exemplos.pt: When I was little, we used to live near the sea.

exemplos.ru: Mis abuelos tenían un huerto.
exemplos.pt: My grandparents used to have a vegetable garden.

erros.motivo: The -ar ending is «-aba», with a «b».
The written accent on «-ía» is required.
The «nosotros» form carries an accent on «-ábamos».
In the imperfecto, verbs that change their vowel in the present don't change it here.
The plural of -er and -ir verbs is «-ían», with an accent.

topicos.titulo: Ser, ir, ver, and when to use the imperfecto
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: only three verbs are irregular in the imperfecto: «ser», «ir», and «ver». STEP 2: «ser» becomes era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran. «Ir» becomes iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban. «Ver» becomes veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían. STEP 3: the accent shows up in «éramos» and «íbamos»; in «veía» it marks the strong «i». STEP 4: the first use is a past habit: «Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo» (every summer we'd go to the village). Sentences like this talk about what used to repeat. STEP 5: the second use is describing people and things in the past: «Mi abuela era alta y llevaba gafas» (my grandmother was tall and wore glasses). STEP 6: the third use is age, time, and weather: «Tenía diez años», «Eran las ocho», «Hacía frío», «Llovía». STEP 7: the fourth use is setting the scene or a state: «La casa estaba en una colina», «Mi tío estaba cansado». STEP 8: in all these cases the fact has no clear beginning or end. For a single, closed-off fact (ayer, el lunes), go back to the indefinido. Lesson 22 covers that choice. STEP 9: in Latin America, «de chico, de chica» is common in place of «de niño, de niña», and «de grande» in place of «de mayor».
topicos.comparacao: English «was/were» and «used to go» map closely onto «era» and «iba» for description and habit, so that part feels familiar. What's new is that Spanish treats age, time, and weather in the past (tenía diez años, eran las ocho, hacía frío) as part of this same imperfecto system — a single grammatical category — where English just uses its ordinary past tense for all of these with no special marking at all («I was ten», «it was eight o'clock», «it was cold»), so there's no verb-shape cue in English to flag this as a distinct use.

exemplos.ru: Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo de mi madre.
exemplos.pt: Every summer we used to go to my mother's hometown.

exemplos.ru: Mi abuelo era alto y siempre llevaba sombrero.
exemplos.pt: My grandfather was tall and always wore a hat.

exemplos.ru: Eran las nueve y hacía mucho calor.
exemplos.pt: It was nine o'clock and it was very hot.

exemplos.ru: Yo tenía siete años y veía la tele con mi hermano.
exemplos.pt: I was seven and I used to watch TV with my brother.

erros.motivo: The imperfecto of «ir» has a «b»: «iba».
«Éramos» carries a written accent.
The accent marks the strong «í».
Age at a point in the past is a description: use the imperfecto «tenía».

erros.errado: Eran las nueve y hizo calor.
erros.certo: Eran las nueve y hacía calor.
erros.motivo: Weather as the backdrop of a scene goes in the imperfecto: «hacía».

topicos.titulo: Mientras and three false friends
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: «mientras» connects two actions that were happening at the same time; the verb goes in the imperfecto on both sides: «Mientras yo cocinaba, mi padre leía» (while I was cooking, my father was reading). STEP 2: «exquisito» doesn't mean «exquisite» in the narrow English sense of finely crafted — it just means delicious, really good, or refined: «La comida era exquisita». To say something's odd or strange, use «raro» or «extraño»: «Es un hombre muy raro». STEP 3: «embarazada» doesn't mean «embarrassed» — it means pregnant: «Mi hermana estaba embarazada». To say «embarrassed», use «avergonzado» or «cortado»: «Estaba muy avergonzada». STEP 4: «antiguo» means old in the sense of historic or long-standing; «viejo» means old in the sense of worn or aged. «Una casa antigua» isn't necessarily run-down. STEP 5: the imperfecto also shows up with time and age, as in the previous section: «Eran las cinco y ya era de noche» (it was five and already dark).
topicos.comparacao: Two of these false friends are genuine traps for an English speaker, just from a different direction than for a Portuguese one: «exquisito» looks like English «exquisite» and does share some of its meaning (refined, very good), but it's used far more broadly in Spanish for anything delicious, which can feel like overkill applied to, say, a sandwich. «Embarazada» looks nothing like English «embarrassed» on the page, so an English speaker is less likely to fall into that one by resemblance — but it's worth knowing precisely because the two words can otherwise seem like they should be related. «Raro» maps cleanly onto English «rare» in spelling but means «odd/strange» far more often than «uncommon» in everyday Spanish.

erros.motivo: «Exquisito» means delicious; «esquisito» isn't a Spanish word.

erros.errado: Mi amiga estaba embarazada de vergüenza.
erros.motivo: «Embarazada» means pregnant; «embarrassed» is «avergonzada» or «cortada».
For something odd, use «raro» or «extraño».

topicos.titulo: Imperfecto for the setting, indefinido for the event
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: think of a story like a movie. First comes the setting: the time, the weather, the place, how people were. Then come the events, one after another. STEP 2: the setting goes in the imperfecto, because it's ongoing with no marked start or end: «Eran las ocho, hacía frío y yo esperaba el autobús» (it was eight, it was cold, and I was waiting for the bus). STEP 3: each event goes in the indefinido, because it starts and ends: «De repente llegó Marta y me saludó» (suddenly Marta arrived and said hello). STEP 4: ask each verb two questions. «Did this happen once and finish?» Then use the indefinido. «Was this ongoing, or how things were at that moment?» Then use the imperfecto. STEP 5: when an ongoing action gets interrupted, the ongoing one goes in the imperfecto and the one that interrupts goes in the indefinido: «Dormía cuando sonó el teléfono» (I was sleeping when the phone rang). STEP 6: a sequence of events, one after another, all stays in the indefinido: «Llegué, abrí la puerta, vi una carta y la leí» (I arrived, opened the door, saw a letter, and read it). STEP 7: the markers help. Indefinido: ayer, un día, aquel día, de repente, el lunes, una vez, a las tres. Imperfecto: siempre, cada día, todos los veranos, de niño, mientras, normalmente. STEP 8: in Spain, for a period that hasn't ended (esta mañana, hoy), the event uses the pretérito perfecto, while the setting stays in the imperfecto: «Esta mañana llovía y he llevado el paraguas». In Latin America people say «Esta mañana llovía y llevé el paraguas».
topicos.comparacao: English's simple past covers both roles here with no change in form at all — «it was raining» (ongoing) and «it rained» (a finished event) are the closest English gets, using «was/were + -ing» versus the plain past, but English speakers routinely blur that line in casual speech. Spanish forces the choice every single time, with two completely different verb forms, so this lesson's two questions — «did it happen once and finish?» versus «was it ongoing or how things were?» — aren't a check on something you already do instinctively; they're a habit to build from scratch.

exemplos.ru: Eran las diez y yo leía cuando oí un ruido.
exemplos.pt: It was ten o'clock and I was reading when I heard a noise.

exemplos.ru: Llovía mucho, así que me quedé en casa.
exemplos.pt: It was raining hard, so I stayed home.

exemplos.ru: Mientras esperaba el tren, perdí el teléfono.
exemplos.pt: While I was waiting for the train, I lost my phone.

exemplos.ru: Un día mi hermano llegó muy contento.
exemplos.pt: One day my brother arrived really happy.

tabela.exemplo: Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo.

tabela.pergunta: Is it a description, time, age, weather?
tabela.exemplo: Eran las ocho y hacía frío.

tabela.pergunta: Was it ongoing when something happened?

erros.motivo: «Ayer» signals a single, finished event, which calls for the indefinido.

erros.errado: De niño fui al pueblo cada verano.
erros.certo: De niño iba al pueblo cada verano.
erros.motivo: A past habit calls for the imperfecto.
The ongoing action is the imperfecto; the one that interrupts is the indefinido.

erros.errado: Llovía y de repente un coche paraba.
erros.certo: Llovía y de repente un coche paró.
erros.motivo: «De repente» marks a single event: indefinido.

topicos.titulo: Sabía × supe, había × hubo, and salir × irse
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: four verbs shift meaning depending on which past tense they're in. «Sabía» means «I already knew»; «supe» means «I found out (at that moment)». «Conocía a Ana» means «I already knew Ana»; «conocí a Ana» means «I met Ana for the first time». STEP 2: «quería salir» means «I wanted to leave», with no word on whether I actually did; «quise salir» means «I tried to leave», and «no quise salir» means «I refused to leave». STEP 3: «podía salir» means «I had the option of leaving»; «pude salir» means «I managed to leave», and «no pude salir» means «I wasn't able to leave». STEP 4: «había» is the imperfecto of «hay» and sets the scene: «Había mucha gente en la plaza» (there were a lot of people in the square). STEP 5: «hubo» is the indefinido of «hay» and reports a specific event: «Hubo un accidente en la plaza» (there was an accident in the square). Both are invariable: «había dos personas», «hubo dos accidentes» — never «habían» or «hubieron». STEP 6: judging a whole, finished event calls for the indefinido: «La fiesta fue genial» (the party was great). Describing how the party was at a given moment calls for the imperfecto: «La fiesta era genial, pero yo estaba cansado» (the party was great, but I was tired). STEP 7: a closed period, even a long one, calls for the indefinido: «Viví tres años en Lima» (I lived in Lima for three years); with no stated limit, the imperfecto: «Vivía en Lima» (I used to live in Lima). STEP 8: «salir de» means to leave a place («Salí del trabajo a las seis»); «irse» means to go away, to take off («Se fue a las seis»); «salir con alguien» means to go out with someone, in the sense of dating («Salió con Marta»).
topicos.comparacao: English has exactly this same split in meaning for «knew/found out» and «could/managed to», so the underlying logic isn't new — «I knew» versus «I found out», «I could leave» versus «I managed to leave» are real, distinct ideas in English too, just expressed with different words rather than a tense swap on the same verb. What's new is «había» versus «hubo»: English «there was» covers both the backdrop sense (there were a lot of people) and the single-event sense (there was an accident) with the exact same words, so nothing in English flags that Spanish treats these as two different grammatical choices.

exemplos.ru: Ya sabía la noticia, pero ayer supe los detalles.
exemplos.pt: I already knew the news, but yesterday I found out the details.

exemplos.ru: Había mucha gente y de repente hubo un accidente.
exemplos.pt: There were a lot of people, and suddenly there was an accident.

exemplos.ru: Quería ir, pero no pude.
exemplos.pt: I wanted to go, but I couldn't manage it.

tabela.indefinido: conocí = met for the first time
quise / no quise = tried to / refused to
pude / no pude = managed to / wasn't able to

erros.errado: Habían muchas personas en la plaza.
erros.certo: Había muchas personas en la plaza.
erros.motivo: «Haber» as existence is impersonal: «había» never changes.
The same goes for «hubo»: it's invariable.

erros.errado: Ayer sabía la noticia. (meaning: I found out)
erros.motivo: For finding out a fact, use the indefinido.

erros.errado: Salí de el trabajo a las seis.
erros.certo: Salí del trabajo a las seis.
erros.motivo: The preposition «de» plus the article «el» contracts to «del».

topicos.titulo: The shape of a narration
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: a good narration has three parts: the setting (imperfecto), the problem or event (indefinido), and the outcome (indefinido). STEP 2: useful connectors: «al principio» opens it, «entonces» and «de repente» move the story forward, «por eso» gives the consequence, and «al final» closes it. STEP 3: the setting can come back in the middle of the story when something needs explaining: «Tenía prisa, porque mi hermana cumplía años» (I was in a hurry, because it was my sister's birthday). STEP 4: the weather follows the same rule. «Llovía mucho» describes the setting; «Llovió toda la noche» sums up a closed period. STEP 5: in Latin America, «parada» and «cumplir años» are understood everywhere; for «bus», some regions say «colectivo», «guagua», or «camión», depending on the country.
topicos.comparacao: English's connectors map onto these almost one for one: «al principio» is «at first», «por eso» is «so» or «that's why», and «al final» is «in the end». Watch the difference between «al final» (in the end, as the story wraps up) and «por fin» (finally, after a wait): «Al final fuimos» (in the end we went) versus «¡Por fin llegó el autobús!» (the bus finally showed up!) — English «finally» can cover both senses, where Spanish keeps them as two separate phrases.

erros.errado: Llovió mucho cuando salí de la oficina.
erros.certo: Llovía mucho cuando salí de la oficina.
erros.motivo: Rain as an ongoing backdrop calls for the imperfecto.
To give the cause, write «porque» as one word.

topicos.titulo: Lo, la, los, las: not repeating the object
topicos.explicacao: STEP 1: the direct object is the thing or person that receives the verb's action. To find it, ask «what?» or «who?» right after the verb: in «Compré el libro», I bought what? El libro. STEP 2: to avoid repeating it, swap the object for a pronoun that agrees with it in gender and number: «lo» (masculine, singular), «la» (feminine, singular), «los» (masculine, plural), and «las» (feminine, plural). «¿Compraste el libro? — Sí, lo compré.» STEP 3: the pronoun comes before the conjugated verb, as its own separate word with no hyphen: «Lo compré», «La veo», «Las busco». STEP 4: in the negative, «no» comes before the pronoun: «No lo tengo», «No la encuentro». STEP 5: with an infinitive, there are two equally correct positions: before the conjugated verb («Lo quiero comprar») or attached to the end of the infinitive («Quiero comprarlo»), with no hyphen. STEP 6: with the pretérito perfecto, the pronoun comes before «haber»: «Lo he visto», «No la he encontrado».
